subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does GNI per capita measure?
options: The literacy rate of adults
The number of births per year
The total population of a country
The average income per person in a country
questions.explain: GNI per capita is the gross national income divided by the population, giving the average income per person.

questions.q: What is 'debt relief' as a strategy to reduce the development gap?
options: Cancelling or reducing the debts a poor country owes
Lending more money to poor countries
Charging higher interest on loans
Forcing a country to repay debt quickly
questions.explain: Debt relief cancels or reduces a country's debt, freeing up money to spend on development such as schools and hospitals.

questions.q: In the Demographic Transition Model, Stage 1 is characterised by:
options: High birth rate and high death rate
Low birth rate and low death rate
Low birth rate and high death rate
Falling death rate and high birth rate
questions.explain: Stage 1 has both high birth and death rates, so the population stays low and stable.

questions.q: What is 'intermediate technology'?
options: Large-scale automated factories
Technology only used in rich countries
Simple, affordable, sustainable technology suited to local needs and skills
The most advanced technology available
questions.explain: Intermediate (appropriate) technology is small-scale and low-cost, such as a hand pump, suited to local resources and skills.

questions.q: Which of these is a physical cause of the development gap?
options: High government investment in schools
A landlocked location or frequent natural hazards
A skilled, well-educated workforce
Good trade links with neighbours
questions.explain: Physical factors such as being landlocked, having a harsh climate or suffering natural disasters can slow development.

questions.q: Which is a benefit a TNC can bring to an emerging country like India or Nigeria?
options: Creating jobs and bringing investment
Reducing the country's exports
Lowering the literacy rate
Removing all local industry
questions.explain: TNCs can create employment, bring investment and skills, and boost exports, helping economic development.

questions.q: How might microfinance loans help reduce the development gap?
options: By cancelling all national debt
By lending small sums to individuals to start small businesses
By giving large loans only to big corporations
By banning small businesses
questions.explain: Microfinance provides small loans to ordinary people, often the poor, so they can start enterprises and improve their incomes.

questions.q: Why can a single indicator like GNI per capita be misleading about development?
options: It is an average and hides inequalities within a country
It only applies to rich countries
It measures life expectancy instead of income
It is always inaccurate
questions.explain: Averages such as GNI per capita hide the gap between rich and poor and say nothing about health or education.

questions.q: A drawback of TNCs investing in an emerging country can be that:
options: They never create any jobs
They only employ local managers
They always pay the highest wages
Profits often go back to the company's home country
questions.explain: Much of a TNC's profit may be sent back to its headquarters abroad rather than staying in the host country.

questions.q: How can fairer trade help reduce the development gap more than aid?
options: It builds long-term, self-sustaining income for producers
It makes countries permanently dependent on donors
It only provides short-term emergency relief
It removes all jobs from poorer countries
questions.explain: Trade builds lasting income and economic independence, whereas some aid can create dependency.

questions.q: As an emerging country such as India develops, its economy typically shifts towards:
options: Manufacturing and growing service industries
Mostly subsistence farming
Reduced industrial output
Hunting and gathering
questions.explain: Industrialisation moves an economy from farming towards manufacturing and services, raising incomes and development.

questions.q: Why do geographers prefer the term 'newly emerging economy (NEE)' for countries like India and Nigeria?
options: They are rapidly industrialising and growing economically
They are the poorest countries in the world
They have stopped developing
They have the same wealth as the UK
questions.explain: NEEs are countries whose economies are growing quickly through industrialisation, moving up from low-income status.

questions.q: Which type of aid is most likely to lead to long-term, sustainable development?
options: Large loans with high interest
One-off cash gifts to governments
Small-scale projects that train local people and use local resources
Short-term emergency food aid only
questions.explain: Bottom-up, small-scale aid that trains people and uses appropriate technology tends to be more sustainable than large top-down aid.

questions.q: How can historical colonialism help explain the development gap?
options: It only ever benefited the colonised countries
Colonised countries often had resources taken and weak economies left behind
It had no effect on modern economies
It made all former colonies wealthy
questions.explain: Colonial powers exploited resources and shaped economies to serve themselves, leaving many former colonies disadvantaged.

questions.q: What is a Transnational Corporation (TNC)?
options: A government-owned charity
A small local business in one town
A company that operates in more than one country
A type of international aid agency
questions.explain: A TNC is a large company with operations, such as factories or offices, in several different countries.

questions.q: How can tourism help a developing country close the development gap?
options: It always damages the economy
It reduces the country's foreign earnings
It removes the need for any other industry
It brings in income and creates jobs
questions.explain: Tourism generates foreign income and creates jobs, which can be invested in services and infrastructure.

questions.q: At which stage of the Demographic Transition Model does population grow most rapidly?
options: Stage 1
Stage 5
Stage 2, when death rates fall but birth rates stay high
Stage 4
questions.explain: In Stage 2 the death rate falls (better healthcare and food) while the birth rate stays high, causing rapid population growth.

questions.q: Investing in education in a developing country helps reduce the development gap because it:
options: Reduces the skills of the workforce
Increases the birth rate sharply
Creates a more skilled workforce able to earn higher incomes
Lowers life expectancy
questions.explain: A better-educated workforce is more productive and can attract investment, raising incomes and standards of living.

questions.q: In the Demographic Transition Model, what happens to the birth rate in Stage 3?
options: It stays very high
It rises sharply
It becomes higher than the death rate
It falls as the death rate stays low
questions.explain: In Stage 3 the birth rate falls (due to contraception, education and lower infant mortality) while the death rate remains low.

questions.q: What does HDI (Human Development Index) measure?
options: The number of doctors in a country
Only the literacy rate
Only a country's income per person
A combination of income, education and life expectancy
questions.explain: HDI is a composite index combining income (GNI per capita), education and life expectancy to give a fuller picture of development.

questions.q: What is 'fair trade'?
options: Trade with no rules or agreements
Selling goods at the lowest possible price
Banning all imports from other countries
A system ensuring producers in poorer countries get a fair, stable price
questions.explain: Fair trade guarantees producers a fair and stable price, helping farmers in developing countries earn a reliable income.

questions.q: Which of these would you expect in a highly developed country?
options: High birth rate and low life expectancy
High death rate and low GNI
High life expectancy and high literacy rate
Low literacy and low life expectancy
questions.explain: More developed countries typically have high life expectancy and literacy rates alongside high incomes.
